title: Maximum output tokens and cost control

videos.script: Every request to a model ends in one of two ways. {{two}} The model chooses to stop, or a limit stops it. {{limit}} The limit is a maximum number of output tokens. It does not ask for a short answer. It cuts the loop when the count is reached, mid-sentence if need be. {{cut}} That makes it two things at once. {{both}} It is the guard against a reply that would run for ever. {{loop}} And it is the most that one request's output can cost. {{cost}} In this lesson you cut toylm's answers short, and watch a cut list read as complete. {{list}} You cut a JSON reply, and watch the validator refuse it. {{json}} Then you price a request with tok, and see the bill move with the limit. {{price}} By the end you check why a reply stopped before you trust it. {{check}}
